newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-SPAIN TO RESTRICT NUMBER OF NON-EU PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPAIN TO RESTRICT NUMBER OF NON-EU PLAYERS.

text.p: The Spanish soccer federation and the Spanish players' association reached an agreement on Friday over the number of non-European Union players allowed to play for leading clubs.
Under the agreement clubs will be allowed to register six "foreign" players and have four on the pitch at any one time.
The move comes amid growing concern among clubs and fans that Spain's talented junior players are not getting enough opportunities to play at top level.
"We have too many foreigners, that's evident," said Gerado Gonzalez Movilla, president of the players' association. "More than two hundred are playing in the first and second divisions."
The number of non-European Union players in Spanish football, particularly from Eastern European and South America, has increased steadily in recent years.
